headline: Binder design expands to multi-variant, atom-level and latent-space objectives with new pose and interface assessment
label: Computational Binder Design
summary: New preprints extend binder design beyond single-target affinity, alongside tools for data generation and for assessing glycan poses and protein interfaces.
synthesis: The dominant thread is binder design conditioned on objectives richer than affinity to one fixed target. Germinal Multi optimizes one paratope across multiple antigen variants, reporting binding to EGFR variants and SARS-CoV-2 neutralization. Pallatom2 models sequence, backbone, side chains and target contacts jointly at atom level (65.9M parameters). The PDZ work designs peptides along directions in a shared latent space learned from affinity prediction. VReceptor simulates sequence-dependent peptide binding data to address data scarcity. Supporting assessment tools include CARVE, which scores glycan pose quality on 1,974 complexes, and TopoPPI, which maps protein-protein interfaces into low-distortion 2D atlases. Modalities and validation standards differ, so results are not directly comparable.
